He's being fired.

meanings.note: Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'мереть'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to die', paired with 'умирать'.

examples.trans: She died last year.
He died very old.
But she died anyway.

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'restaurant', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Давайте сделаем в нашем ресторане праздник Хэллоуин!
examples.trans: Let's hold a Halloween celebration in our restaurant!

examples.text: Ведь праздник Хэллоуин вообще предложил вам я!
examples.trans: After all, I was the one who suggested the Halloween party to you!

meanings.note: the plural is a different word: люди, людям, о людях
Plural люди, a different word. Common masculine noun meaning 'person; (pl) people' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: He is a good person.
There are a lot of people here.
I know the problems of ordinary people.

meanings.note: Чуть-чуть = a tiny bit. Core Russian adv meaning 'a little; nearly' in everyday speech.
чуть не + verb: я чуть не упал = I nearly fell

examples.trans: I nearly fell.
Wait a little.

examples.text: Садись, не бойся. Я ведь сам чуть тебя не отпустил.
examples.trans: Sit down, don't be afraid. I very nearly let you go myself.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'I' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I'm doing my homework.
I grew up here.
Chef, I didn't take it.
